executiveSummary:
Momentum remains positive with strong ARR growth (70%), healthy unit economics (CAC 0.56; LTV:CAC 6.5), and improving operating leverage (EBIT from -21% to 8% by Dec 27). However, retention is the primary drag: logo retention 85%, gross 79%, and 12‑month NRR trending down to ~92%, all below typical SaaS benchmarks. Budget execution is broadly on track (ARR +11% vs budget; EBITDA modestly ahead) but General costs are materially over budget. Growth mix is land-led: new ARR outpaces expansion (12‑month waterfall: Land 4.32M vs Expand 0.71M; recent 3 months: New 720 vs Expand 180), and upsell is 6% under budget.

  • Management focus 1: Retention and NRR recovery — address logo losses and downsell pressure to lift gross/net retention.
  • Management focus 2: Cost discipline in G&A — correct the annual overspend while preserving improving EBIT trajectory.
  • Management focus 3: Expansion acceleration — increase upsell/expansion to rebalance growth away from predominantly new logos.
page1:
Overall health shows efficient growth but retention and profitability remain the limiting factors. ARR is £9.4M with 70% growth; Rule of 40 is 63% supported by 78% gross margin and strong CAC efficiency (0.56). Offsetting this, logo retention (85%), gross retention (79%), and net retention (90%) are weak, and EBIT is still negative (-7%) despite improving cost mix (S&M 37%, Dev 28%, G&A 20%).

  • Management focus: Prioritise retention lift to move NRR back toward benchmark while maintaining CAC discipline to drive EBIT to positive territory.
page2:
Growth engine is balanced between steady new logos and improving retention in the latest quarter. Dec 27 quarter delivered ARR 17,646 (+1,502 net; +43%), with 16 new logos and 3 lost; expansion £467, downsell -£90, attrition -£315, and net retention at 102% (up from sub-100% troughs earlier). Deal volume remains healthy (2,098), and logo count has scaled from 68 to 168 since Mar 25.

  • Context: Despite the latest uptick, historical variability in logo retention (81–100%) indicates retention remains a core risk to sustain growth.
  • Management focus: Strengthen post‑sale retention to stabilise logo churn and protect ARR retained.
page3:
Operating leverage is improving as revenue scales from 1,687 to 4,455 and EBIT moves from -360 to 359 (margin -21% to 8%) by Dec 27, aided by declining S&M % (45% to 24%) while gross margin holds ~78–79%. CAC remains efficient (~0.51–0.88) and LTV:CAC rose to 15.2. Headcount expanded to 106, concentrated in Development (53). Rule of 40 improved to 51%.

  • Context: Positive EBIT in recent quarters suggests a credible path to sustained profitability if cost discipline is maintained.
  • Management focus: Rein in General costs, which trend upward alongside scale, to protect margin gains.
page4:
ARR is diversified but retention pressure is evident. 12‑month waterfall shows growth led by Land (£4.32M) with modest Expand (£0.71M) and losses from downsell/attrition (-£1.15M). NRR on a rolling 12‑month basis declined to ~92%. Verticals are led by Energy & Utilities (£3.99M) and Life Science (£2.50M); regions are balanced with South America (£2.32M), Asia (£2.09M), Africa (£1.95M), North America (£1.91M), and Europe (£1.42M).

  • Context: Total gross retention at 79% and NRR ~90–92% sit below common SaaS benchmarks (GRR ~85–95%, NRR ~100%+), implying value at risk without retention/expansion uplift.
  • Management focus: Target expansion in existing accounts (especially larger verticals) and address churn cohorts driving the NRR decline.
page5:
Recent movements are encouraging but still land‑heavy. Last 3 months netted +£855 ARR: New £720 across 13 logos and regions (notably South America £270, Africa £180, North America £270, Asia £90), Expand £180, and Downsells -£45 (Africa). By industry, Energy & Utilities (£360 new; £90 expand) and Government (£270 new) led additions.

  • Context: The mix skews to new logos (84% of net adds), consistent with the 12‑month pattern of land‑led growth.
  • Management focus: Convert recent lands into near‑term expansions to strengthen NRR and reduce reliance on new logo volume.
page6:
Execution versus budget is broadly favorable. Annual ARR is +11% vs budget (additions +8%, attrition better by 12%, downsell worse by 9%, upsell -6%). P&L: revenue +1%, margin -1%, with lower S&M and Development spend offset by higher General (-38% vs budget). EBITDA is modestly ahead annually (+£30, +5%) and more so in the latest quarter/month.

  • Context: The overspend in General masks otherwise disciplined delivery and is the primary variance driver on the cost side.
  • Management focus: Correct General cost overruns and preserve S&M/Dev efficiency to sustain EBITDA outperformance.
